key_insight: WC–Co–Cr coating performance depends on powder morphology and spray method: detonation spraying favors hardness, while HVOF yields dense, uniform coatings with low friction.
engineering_relevance: Selecting the powder and deposition process can improve coating suitability for machine parts exposed to intensive friction and high loads.
method: Compared detonation-sprayed and HVOF WC–Co–Cr coatings.
Examined feedstock morphology, coating microstructure, and composition using SEM and EDS.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an average microhardness of 1449 HV for detonation-sprayed coatings and a friction coefficient of Kt = 0.143 for HVOF coatings.
watch_item: Test conditions, variability, and quantitative wear rates are not provided in the abstract, limiting direct translation to service-life predictions.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
